findings.title: Queries are interpolated a second time when shard splitting delegates to runSplitQuery
findings.body: runSplitQuery now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables on every target. shardQuerySplitting.ts already interpolates its targets in runShardSplitQuery (line 52) and then calls runSplitQuery(datasource, subRequest, ...) with the already-interpolated and shard-selector-injected expressions (shardQuerySplitting.ts line 163). Those expressions are interpolated again here. Any value that survives the first pass and contains a '$' (regex anchors, literal dollar signs in label values, escaped variable-like text) can be rewritten a second time, so the query sent to Loki can differ from what the user wrote. Interpolation should happen in exactly one place for each request path.

findings.title: Test asserts applyTemplateVariables is called 5 times, locking in redundant double interpolation
findings.body: The updated expectation `expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` counts the calls made by runShardSplitQuery plus the repeated calls made inside runSplitQuery for each shard sub-request. The test encodes the redundant interpolation as expected behaviour, so it will fail to catch the double-interpolation regression, and it will break if the redundancy is correctly removed. The test should assert the observable query text sent to runQuery rather than the number of interpolation calls.

findings.title: $__range detection now runs on interpolated expressions, so range-variable queries may be split
findings.body: querySupportsSplitting checks isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr) to avoid splitting queries that use $__range, because $__range must be evaluated over the full request range. Interpolation now runs before this check (line 299), so the check sees the expression after applyTemplateVariables has rewritten it. If interpolation replaces or removes the $__range token, the check no longer matches and such queries get split, which is the exact case the guard was meant to prevent. The ordering needs to be verified, and the detection should run on the original expression or the test suite should cover a $__range query through runSplitQuery. No test in querySplitting.test.ts covers this path.
